headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while the week is red, and the whales keep filing onto exchanges anyway
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's a clean one for once: five of seven majors here, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB, are above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses in place. DOGE and ADA are the exceptions, both below trend and both un-crossed. That's a market where the broad structure still leans constructive, even though the tape underneath it is bruised. Bitcoin is up 0.4% on the day but down 5.5% on the week and up 18.4% on the month, that's the shape of a coin that ran hard over four weeks and has spent the last seven days giving some of it back. Every asset in this set shows that same day-up, week-down, month-up split, which tells you the pullback is a week-scale event sitting inside a month-scale advance, not a reversal of the longer trend, at least not yet.

Momentum agrees with that reading of a rest, not an acceleration. RSI-14 across the board sits in the mid-40s to low-50s, BTC at 49.1, ETH at 50.4, SOL at 49.0, XRP at 45.9: textbook neutral, no asset overbought or oversold. MACD is below signal on every single one of them, including the names still above their 200-day average. That's a real divergence worth naming: price structure says uptrend, momentum says the trend has gone quiet or is rolling over short-term. When trend and momentum disagree like this, it usually means the move is digesting rather than reversing, but it's not proof of either.

Positioning adds a wrinkle. BTC funding on OKX is a modest 0.0058% per 8 hours (6.4% annualized), positive but not hot, positive funding means longs are paying shorts to hold their bet, so the crowd is leaning long but not aggressively. The long/short account ratio of 1.78 confirms more accounts are long than short. What's notable is the liquidation mix: over the last 5 hours, BTC shorts absorbed $1.24M in liquidations against just $138.6K for longs, a lopsided flush that lines up with the day's small green print squeezing out short bets. SOL and XRP funding are negative (-6.1% and -5.4% annualized respectively), meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual setup where the crowd is skewed long by ratio (2.38 and 2.99) but the marginal bet is priced against them. DOGE stands out with the richest funding at 10.1% annualized and a long/short ratio of 4.68, about as crowded and expensive as this board gets.

Flows are where the story gets genuinely tense. BTC spot ETFs posted a net outflow of $288.7M on 15 Sep 2026, and the five-session net is a deeper outflow of $544.9M, same direction both windows, so call that a real short-run trend in the traditional-finance bid. ETH ETFs disagree with themselves: a $56.7M outflow on the same day sits against a $285.6M net inflow over five sessions, which means one bad day interrupted an otherwise positive week, not the reverse. Whale activity over the last 24 hours shows $48.2M in net value moving onto exchanges, with BTC alone contributing $76.9M onto Binance (partly offset by CRO moving off exchanges). Zoom out and the weekly whale series has shown money moving onto exchanges in every one of the last four weeks tracked, from $1,199M (week ending Aug 26) down to $49M (Sep 02), back up to $406M (Sep 09), and $558M (week ending Sep 16). Coins moving toward exchanges while ETF flows also lean negative on BTC is two supply-side signals pointing the same way, worth sitting with. Stablecoin float, meanwhile, grew a modest 1.07% over 30 days to $309.5B, dry powder building slowly rather than surging.

Sentiment is sitting at 51, dead neutral, within a 30-day range of 41 to 74, so the crowd isn't panicking and isn't euphoric either, it's shrugged. That's actually consistent with a market where price is flat-to-up on the day, red on the week, and green on the month: nobody's sure which window to believe. What to watch from here: whether BTC ETF outflows extend a sixth session or reverse, whether the weekly whale-flow series posts its first net inflow after four straight weeks onto exchanges, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on BTC or ETH, which would resolve the momentum-versus-trend divergence in the bulls' favor rather than leave it hanging.
